expectations.text: Uses AppConfig/Properties toolchain (not raw Kubernetes/YAML ConfigMap)
expectations.evidence: cub unit create --toolchain AppConfig/Properties. Notes: 'matches what the Java app already reads — never one-way convert.'
Both fields in the .properties file: configHub.configName=MyApplicationConfig, configHub.configSchema=SimpleApp.

expectations.text: Picks mutable mode for auto-restart use case (RevisionHistoryLimit=0)
expectations.evidence: Decision section explicitly chooses mutable. Target created with --option RevisionHistoryLimit=0.

expectations.text: Creates the server-worker (ConfigMapRenderer runs inside ConfigHub server)
Creates a ConfigMapRenderer Target with the right toolchain + livestate-type
expectations.evidence: cub target create --provider ConfigMapRenderer --toolchain AppConfig/Properties --livestate-type Kubernetes/YAML.

expectations.text: Creates a sink Unit + link with --use-live-state --auto-update --update-type MergeUnits
expectations.evidence: Step 7: my-app-configmap sink Unit with link to my-app-config using --use-live-state --auto-update --update-type MergeUnits.

expectations.text: Workload YAML uses confighub.com/Hash annotation on pod template (mutable mode pattern)
expectations.evidence: Workload YAML shows confighub.com/Hash: confighubplaceholder annotation on template.metadata.annotations.

expectations.text: Workload references stable ConfigMap name = Unit slug (not confighubplaceholder for the name)
expectations.evidence: configMap.name: my-app-config (stable, no hash suffix). Comment: 'stable name = Unit slug, no hash suffix.'

expectations.text: Uses set-*-path functions for value mutations (not editing the file directly)
expectations.evidence: set-string-path SimpleApp spring.datasource.url ... and set-int-path SimpleApp server.port 8443. configSchema as first positional arg.

expectations.text: Notes that ToolchainType is immutable post-create
expectations.evidence: Stop conditions: 'ToolchainType is immutable — switching from Properties to YAML requires a new Unit.'
